features.name: Academic preparation
features.description: The level of formal technical education or academic credential the letter presents as preparation for the role.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree, equivalent, or no advanced degree is presented.
Master's degree is presented.
Doctoral degree is presented.

features.name: Agentic systems architecture
features.description: The depth of direct experience designing agent-based systems, especially around autonomy boundaries, control planes, permissions, and guardrails.

levels.descriptor: No agent-based tooling experience is shown.
The letter mentions agents or autonomous workflows only in general terms.
The letter describes a recognizable agent architecture, typically pairing Python agents with Go services.
The letter shows deliberate control design for agents, such as permissions, auditability, bounded actions, or explicit end-to-end ownership.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Whether the letter demonstrates practical command of data structures and algorithms through concrete engineering examples.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Algorithmic fluency is claimed, but without a concrete example.
At least one specific redesign or optimization shows applied algorithmic thinking.
Multiple or especially vivid examples show data structures and algorithms materially shaping system design.

features.name: Applied AI maturity
features.description: Whether the applicant has shipped AI-backed systems in production and understands reliability, evaluation, and failure-mode handling.

levels.descriptor: No AI evidence.
Only vague, aspirational, or lightly specified AI mention.
Shows concrete experience shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality.
Shows concrete production AI work plus explicit evaluation, guardrails, correctness, or failure-mode management.

features.name: Developer enablement orientation
features.description: Whether the letter frames security tooling as serving internal developers by reducing friction, improving defaults, and making secure behavior easier.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: How consistently the letter backs claims with concrete systems, mechanisms, quantities, or examples rather than generic assertions.

levels.descriptor: Mostly offers generic assertions or checklist-style requirement matching.
Provides some specifics, but major claims remain abstract or unsubstantiated.
Gives several concrete, role-relevant examples showing what was built or changed.
Repeatedly backs claims with precise mechanisms, context, and outcomes that make the applicant's contribution easy to picture.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: How strongly the letter establishes Go as a meaningful production language in the applicant's recent backend work.

levels.descriptor: Does not provide meaningful evidence of Go use.
Mentions some Go exposure but not as a core language.
Presents Go as a major working language in production.
Presents Go as the principal or dominant language across core services.

features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: How clearly the letter states the results or operational effects of the applicant's work rather than only listing activities.

levels.descriptor: Lists responsibilities or technologies without explaining what changed because of the work.
Suggests benefit, but the outcome remains vague or implied.
Gives a clear before-and-after or operational result, such as a queue becoming routed, a bottleneck disappearing, or hours being saved.
Shows strong leverage-oriented impact articulation, tying the work to measurable capacity, broad downstream benefit, or a transformed operating model.

features.name: Language breadth
features.description: The range of programming languages the letter presents beyond the role's core required language.

levels.descriptor: Shows narrow breadth beyond the main language or two.
Shows moderate breadth across several additional languages.
Shows very broad breadth across many additional languages.

features.name: Narrative voice and cohesion
features.description: How memorable, coherent, and well-shaped the letter's overall voice, framing, and flow are beyond a templated qualifications list.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like an interchangeable template or a flat list of qualifications.
The letter is competent but generic, with limited individuality in framing or voice.
The letter has a distinctive opening, viewpoint, or sustained framing device.
The letter is memorable and cohesive, with a clear throughline linking the opening idea, past work, and motivation for this role.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Whether the applicant shows ongoing attacker-oriented skill-building through CTFs or other offensive-security practice.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-practice evidence is mentioned.
Mentions casual or occasional participation with little detail.
Shows regular participation presented as deliberate skill maintenance.
Shows strong results or serious competitive commitment that signals sustained offensive practice.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: The degree of responsibility the applicant shows in contributing to or maintaining public codebases used by others.

levels.descriptor: No open-source activity is mentioned.
Mentions occasional patches or minor contributions.
Shows regular contributions or maintainership of a small project.
Maintains a project with outside users or community responsibilities such as reviews, releases, issue handling, or roadmap decisions.

features.name: Ownership level
features.description: How directly the letter presents the applicant as the person with primary responsibility, autonomy, or end-to-end ownership over the work described.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads mostly as passive, resume-like claims with little direct ownership.
The letter shows some first-person ownership, but mainly on isolated tasks or narrow pieces of work.
The letter uses clear builder language around multiple shipped systems, automations, or redesigns.
The letter repeatedly shows end-to-end ownership, architecture, delivery, and ongoing operational responsibility.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: How technically ambitious and substantial the applicant's self-directed projects appear outside normal work duties.

levels.descriptor: No side project is mentioned, or the example is very small and shows little technical challenge.
A modest personal project is described, showing completion but limited system complexity.
A substantial project is described, involving meaningful systems design, edge cases, or failure handling.
An especially ambitious project is described, such as a distributed or production-like system built to explore hard engineering problems deeply.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Whether the applicant is motivated by building shared foundational systems whose impact compounds across many teams or products.

levels.descriptor: The motivation could fit almost any software role and does not emphasize leverage.
The letter mentions scale or infrastructure briefly, but not as a core value.
The letter clearly values foundational tooling, secure defaults, or improvements inherited by many teams.
The letter builds a sustained case around organization-wide multiplier effects and the appeal of high-leverage platform work.

features.name: Production engineering experience
features.description: The depth of relevant professional experience building, shipping, operating, testing, and maintaining real production software systems.

levels.descriptor: Only minimal relevant experience is conveyed, with short tenure, narrow scope, or ambiguous ownership.
Clear early-career production experience is shown, but the record is still limited in depth or breadth.
Solid production background is shown through several years of work with repeated launch and maintenance responsibility.
Extensive directly relevant background is shown through long tenure plus broad multi-service responsibility.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: How substantial and production-oriented the applicant's Python experience appears for services, tooling, automation, or agents.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or appears only incidentally.
Python is mentioned as a tool or companion language, but depth is unclear.
The letter shows regular production Python use for tooling, automation, prototypes, or services.
Python is portrayed as a major production language with broad, concrete use across services, automation, and agent behavior.

features.name: Reliability and maintainer mindset
features.description: Whether the applicant emphasizes correctness, maintainability, failure handling, and long-term operability as core engineering values.

levels.descriptor: Shows little sign of care for maintainability, testing, or long-term operation.
Mentions maintenance or correctness only generically.
Explicitly emphasizes dependable systems, careful engineering, or maintainer habits.
Shows multiple reinforcing signals such as typed or tested tooling, careful releases, production standards, or pride in quiet reliability.

features.name: Role alignment and motivation
features.description: How clearly the letter explains why this specific role is the right next step and maps the applicant's background to its stated responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: Could fit many software roles and mostly reads as a generic application.
Shows some interest in security, backend work, or Google, but the motivation remains fairly broad.
Clearly connects the applicant's interests to one or two responsibilities of this role.
Uses a distinctive framing and threads it through the letter to make the fit with this role feel specific and convincing.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: The extent of hands-on experience performing structured security reviews, assessments, or remediation verification.

levels.descriptor: No real security assessment experience is shown.
Mentions security review in generic or limited terms.
Shows clear assessment work such as threat modeling, code review, or validation of fixes.
Shows repeated or cross-stack assessment practice with a clear method or engineering mindset.

features.name: Security automation framing
features.description: How well the letter understands the job as scaling security work through automation, triage tooling, and workflow leverage rather than generic software engineering.

levels.descriptor: The letter shows little understanding of the specific security problem this team solves.
The letter shows general interest in security engineering, but mostly at a broad level.
The letter clearly articulates goals like reducing manual security work or making the secure path easier for developers.
The letter shows nuanced insight into bottlenecks such as scarce expert attention, vulnerability triage, lifecycle embedding, bounded agents, or similar operational realities.

features.name: Security commitment and philosophy
features.description: Whether the letter conveys a mature, personally committed philosophy of security engineering as proactive, collaborative, and secure-by-default work.

levels.descriptor: Little sign of a security-specific philosophy or perspective.
Expresses seriousness about security, but only in generic terms.
Shows a clear personal lens such as attacker thinking, builder's-eye reviewing, or preference for quiet resilience.
Presents a memorable, role-relevant philosophy that convincingly shapes how the applicant builds and evaluates systems.

features.name: Security credentials
features.description: The strength of formal third-party security certifications or other explicit credential signals cited in the letter.

levels.descriptor: No security certification is mentioned.
A foundational certification such as Security+ is cited.
A hands-on practical certification such as OSCP is cited.

features.name: Vulnerability automation
features.description: Direct experience building tooling that automates vulnerability intake, classification, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or related workflows.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not describe vulnerability-handling automation.
The letter mentions security automation in general, but not a specific vulnerability triage workflow.
The letter shows direct experience automating intake, classification, routing, or deduplication of vulnerability reports.
The letter shows a clear transformation of a manual vulnerability workflow or explicitly states operational impact from the automation.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: The degree of proofreading, grammatical accuracy, and surface-level cleanliness in the letter's prose.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors repeatedly interrupt reading or seriously undermine credibility.
Noticeable proofreading problems distract the reader more than once.
Contains some typos, but the letter remains easy to follow.
Mostly clean, with at most a minor slip.
Polished and effectively error-free at a professional standard.

other.name: Other
other.description: This captures the highest formal technical education explicitly presented in the letter.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree or technical education is stated clearly.
States a bachelor's degree or equivalent.
States a master's degree.
States a doctoral degree or PhD.
